slides.title: Your DB already caches in RAM. So why add **Redis?**
slides.text: The gap is not where you think 👉

slides.title: A warm database is **also in memory**
bullets: 🔥|Hot rows are served from RAM already
🎯|So "RAM vs disk" is not the real difference

cols.title: 🗄 Database read
cols.text: Parse SQL, plan, execute, MVCC checks, locks, build result.

cols.title: ⚡ Redis GET
cols.text: Parse tiny message, one hash lookup, reply.

slides.title: Caching is **not free**
bullets: 🕰️|Stale data: cache can disagree with the DB
🧩|One more system to run and monitor
🌊|Cold cache sends a burst to the DB

slides.title: Say this in 1 line
slides.text: A warm DB is also in RAM. Redis wins by doing **far less work per request** (no planner, no MVCC, **O(1) lookup**), but the **network round trip** usually dominates, so cache hot data and **measure the hit ratio**.
